block_and_edge_counts.interpretation: The retail tools agree exactly at 21 blocks/29 edges. The candidate's radare2 graph is 6 blocks and 12 edges larger. The delta is accounted for by the two candidate-only guards, the GCC loop/switch lowering, and the shared epilogue; it is not a claim of CFG equality.

dispatch_order.retail: cmp message,0x1C: ja high, je WM_ACTIVATEAPP. Low (<=0x1C): message-1 == 0 -> return 0; message-2 == 0 -> WM_DESTROY; else DefWindowProcA. High (>0x1C): message-0x104 == 0 -> WM_SYSKEYDOWN; message-0x105 == 0 -> WM_SYSKEYUP; else DefWindowProcA.
dispatch_order.candidate: cmp message,0x1C: je WM_ACTIVATEAPP, jbe low. High (>0x1C): 0x104 then 0x105, else default. Low (<=0x1C): 0x0001 then 0x0002, else default.
dispatch_order.verdict: same partition constant and same message-to-branch mapping. The two sub-tests are disjoint (0x0001/0x0002 versus 0x0104/0x0105), so the candidate's opposite lexical order for the two sub-tests cannot change any dispatch outcome.

branch_constants.verdict: identical values; only the comparison instruction shape differs (cmp/ja/je + dec versus cmp/je/jbe).

chain_walk.retail: head = [0x5C8DF0]; next = [head]; if next == 0 skip; call [head+8]; if EAX == 0 return 0; head = next; next = [next]; repeat while next != 0.
chain_walk.candidate: head = [0x5D5C70]; if head == 0 skip (candidate-only); next = [head]; if next == 0 skip; call [head+8] only if non-null (candidate-only); if EAX == 0 return 0; head = next; next = [next]; repeat while next != 0.
chain_walk.verdict: same call order and same stop condition on the successor pointer; the two guards are the only added decisions.

scalar_score.reason: Binary Ninja and radare2 operate on different images here (retail 0x400000-based PE and candidate 0x400000-based PE with a different section layout and function VA 0x41F970). The manifest's cfg_similarity 1.0 is the gate's retail-only Binary Ninja-versus-radare2 score, recomputed from the two retail artifacts; it is not candidate equivalence.
